title: An Updated Systematic Review of Routine Outcome Measures for Use in Couple Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper updates MacIntosh and Butters' previous systematic review of outcome measures used in couple therapy. EMBASE, PubMed, PsychINFO, CINAHL and ERIC databases were searched from January 2012 to November 2025 for couple therapy outcome studies. Eight hundred and twenty‐three records were screened; 320 full texts were assessed for eligibility; and 24 papers were selected for review. Selected studies were published in 17 different journals. The journals that published the greatest number of selected studies were the Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology , and the International Journal of Fertility and Sterility. The studies were conducted in nine countries, with the greatest number being conducted in the USA and Iran. A total of 1362 couples participated in the 24 studies in this review. Twenty were randomised controlled trials. Relationship distress was the most common primary presenting problem, and other main concerns were sexual dissatisfaction, infidelity, infertility, cancer‐related distress, substance and alcohol use, anxiety, depression, PTSD, gambling and child abuse. Behavioural couple therapy and emotionally focused couple therapy were the most commonly evaluated models. The Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS), used in over half of the reviewed studies, was the most frequently used measure of relationship satisfaction and couple relational functioning to evaluate couple therapy. Twenty‐one other measures of couple functioning were used, and each in only one study. The Beck Depression inventory was the most frequently used measure of individual functioning.
